# Results — Study 798 (Deferred-Revenue Signal)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **growth in
deferred revenue / contract liabilities leads future sales and forward returns** for
subscription/SaaS-type firms. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python
examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar
month; the partial current month is dropped). Prices fingerprint `f8a44ad79534` (yfinance daily
adjusted closes); events cache = 1,238 (ticker, filing) rows.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **40** subscription/SaaS-type US names that report a current deferred-revenue / contract-liability balance on EDGAR (fixed, current survivors) |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: `DeferredRevenueCurrent` (older filers) → `ContractWithCustomerLiabilityCurrent` (ASC-606, post-2018), longest per-name history; de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **1,238** deferred-revenue quarters, period ends **2009-11-27 → 2026-04-30**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 40 names, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `defrev_yoy` = current-quarter deferred-revenue balance ÷ same quarter a year earlier − 1 |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh signals into **terciles**, long top / short bottom, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** The monthly cross-section grows from ≈9 names in 2010-11 to
≈27 by 2025 as the pure-play SaaS cohort (SNOW, DDOG, CRWD, NET, ZM…) IPO's in 2018-2020.
Terciles on a single-digit cross-section early in the sample are noisy by construction. No
survivorship correction: the basket is current survivors — named on the Signal axis.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does deferred-revenue growth predict returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `defrev_yoy`, one execution lag, 2010-04 → 2026-06
(**195 months**, avg cross-section 19.6 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **+56.2 bps/month** (+6.74%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | +1.04 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **+0.94** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | 0.26 |
| monthly hit rate | 55% |
| long leg / short leg | +230.3 / +174.1 bps/month |
| growth of \$1 (gross) | ×1.72 over 195 months |

The point estimate is **right-signed and economically chunky (~+6.7%/yr gross)**, but it **does
not clear the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** on the autocorrelation-robust statistic (**NW *t* = +0.94**),
nor even on the naïve one-sample *t* (+1.04). A staleness-120 variant is materially the same
(+50.8 bps, NW *t* = +0.84). The **asset-scaled** variant `(ΔDeferredRevenue)/Assets` is the
strongest specification and still falls short: +75.9 bps/month, **NW *t* = +1.63**.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (534-style tercile sort by signal)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `defrev_yoy`; top-minus-bottom forward drift, entered one
day after the filing:

| horizon | n | top | bottom | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 1,232 | +1.25% | +1.54% | **−0.29%** | −0.42 | 48% | 0.66 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 1,213 | +5.70% | +5.37% | **+0.33%** | +0.20 | 49% | 0.41 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 1,185 | +10.15% | +9.62% | **+0.53%** | +0.22 | 47% | 0.41 |

Flat. The tercile means are **non-monotone** (63 d: +5.37% / +5.12% / +5.70% low→high), the
long-short *t* never exceeds +0.22, and the label-shuffle placebo *p* sits around 0.4-0.7 — a
random tercile split beats the real one four times in ten. There is **no forward-return sort**
in this signal on this tape.

## Era split — no regime rescues it

Calendar long-short, split at 2019-01-01 (when the SaaS cohort widens the panel):

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010-2018 | 105 | +53.3 bps | +0.86 |
| 2019-2026 | 90 | +59.6 bps | +0.55 |

Both eras carry the same right-signed-but-insignificant positive; neither clears the bar. The
signal is not "arbitraged away recently" — it never certified in the first place.

## The mechanism, though, is real — deferred revenue **does** lead future sales

Pooled OLS of **next quarter's** YoY revenue growth on this quarter's deferred-revenue growth
(n = 917 matched events):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope *b* | **+0.434** |
| *t* (iid-pooled) | **+27.05** |
| R² | 0.444 |
| Pearson correlation | **+0.667** |
| future sales growth, top deferred-growth tercile | **+40.4%** |
| future sales growth, bottom deferred-growth tercile | **+8.4%** |
| tercile spread in future sales growth | **+32.0 pp** |

Deferred-revenue growth is a **bulletproof lead on future recognised sales** — top-tercile
deferred-growth names go on to grow revenue **+32 percentage points** faster than bottom-tercile
names over the next quarter, correlation +0.67. (The pooled *t* ignores quarter clustering, so
read the magnitude — an economically enormous, mechanical accounting lead — not the literal
+27.) The accounting claim is confirmed; the *market* simply already prices it, which is why the
return spread is a null.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + signal panel with a TUNABLE planted lead (high-deferred-growth names drift
up); no network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **−0.35** (sd 1.08), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **1/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 798) | **+6.56** (mean +236.8 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (one borderline crossing in twelve HAC *t*'s, ~as expected
by chance) and lights up hard on a planted lead. The real-tape NW *t* = +0.94 is therefore a
genuine near-null, not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited
in support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.10):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | +49.9 bps/mo | +5.99%/yr | +0.83 | 0.23 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | +43.7 bps/mo | +5.24%/yr | +0.73 | 0.20 |

Costs barely dent the point estimate (turnover is low — a slow quarterly balance-sheet signal),
but that is moot: the edge is **statistically indistinguishable from zero before any costs are
charged**. You cannot get paid for a spread you cannot certify.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The forward-return long-short is **right-signed and ~+6.7%/yr gross**, and
  the asset-scaled variant reaches **NW *t* = +1.63**, so there is a whiff of the effect the
  literature describes — but it **never clears *t* = 2** (primary NW *t* = +0.94, one-sample
  +1.04), the pooled event drift is **flat and non-monotone** (long-short *t* ≈ +0.2, placebo
  *p* ≈ 0.4), and neither era certifies. Literature-supported, tape-uncertified — the desk's
  definition of `WEAK`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Not certifiable even gross (NW *t* < 1); net of realistic
  long-short costs + borrow it is +0.73 to +0.83 *t*, Sharpe ≈ 0.2. No paycheck.
- **"Does deferred revenue lead future sales?" — CONFIRMED.** The accounting mechanism is real
  and strong (correlation +0.67, top-minus-bottom tercile **+32 pp** of next-quarter sales
  growth). The lead exists; the market already prices it, so it does **not** convert into a
  forward-return edge. Real information, no alpha.
